lede: The biggest thing on the calendar this week is Monday's Norwood Planning and Zoning Commission meeting, where the town takes up Phase I of its Land Use Code rewrite — the kind of foundational change that sets the rules on development and density for years to come. Alongside that, Tuesday is dense with decisions: Town Council holds public hearings on converting two affordable units at 215 East Colorado from price-capped ownership to employee dwelling units, the School Board votes on resolutions backing Proposition NN and Amendment 87 plus second-reading policy approvals, and the Housing Authority takes up the same deed-restriction conversion. Tuesday the BOCC continues its public hearing on adopting updated international building codes and hashes out 2027 nonprofit funding allocations.

notable.stake: Phase I Land Use Code amendments up for formal adoption — sets Norwood's development rules.
Board votes on ballot measure resolutions and second-reading policy approvals.
Resolution would convert two affordable ownership units, removing their maximum sale price.
Public hearings on deed-restriction conversion stripping price caps from two town housing units.
Commission weighs leak forgiveness requests and a new fee that formalizes system cost recovery.
Continued public hearing on new building codes and 2027 nonprofit funding allocation decisions.
